title: Enable IP forwarding for internet sharing
summary: Enable packet forwarding in the kernel to allow the Linux machine to route traffic between the internet interface and the client interface. This is required for internet sharing.

steps.explain:
Edit the sysctl configuration file (e.g., /etc/sysctl.d/30-ipforward.conf) and add the following lines to enable IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding persistently:
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding = 1
net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1

rollback.explain: Remove the added lines from the sysctl configuration file and reboot, or set the values to 0 using sysctl -w.

warnings: Enabling IP forwarding without a properly configured firewall is a security risk.
To make these changes persistent across reboots, you must edit /etc/sysctl.d/30-ipforward.conf or similar.
